# Milestone 7 work packages

The packages of `docs/TechnicalSpec-M7.md` (§31), briefed in turn for the owner's approval
and launched on his word. The head rules of `M7b-WorkPackages.md` hold (each item an intent
with the lead's reading of a way, the intent binding; the budget the owner's; nothing under
`docs/agents/consent/` or in `docs/agents/ConsentBrief.md` touched but by the package the
specification names; no model identifier in any file of the repository; a world order never
shown as sent; the recorded passages' pins re-measured only where a change moves them, with
the old figure beside the new and the reason in the tuning notes; never a test skipped,
disabled or quarantined; a section in the tuning notes and a report to the lead; the lead
plays each merged package briefly and files the notes), and this milestone adds its own
(spec M7's rules 1 to 7: damage is just state; a gun is served by the bill; recognition
before fire; rules first, models welcome; the far ships fight as the near do, coarsely;
realism, not pacing; nothing pre-defines a battle's timing), and from 2026-11-06 decision
64: **every nation-specific extension includes Spain and the relevant Mediterranean factions
where it can** (the signal books, the doctrines, the fighting habits, the regimes, the
nation-keyed tables), a builder writing Spain's row with its source or saying in the tuning
notes what was looked for and not found (spec M7 §28; the Spanish sources in
`docs/design/VesselReferences-2026-11-Spanish.md`).

**How the packages are run (the owner, 2026-10-23).** Milestone 7b is frozen open beside
this milestone (decision 51); its remaining work is wrapped up alongside. **The Fable
packages run one at a time**, so that the owner can meter the week's usage, and each is
**generously scoped and encouraged**: the brief binds the intent and names the ground, and
the builder is free to design and build to the intent as it judges best, taking an item
another way with its reason, growing a part where the work shows it should, and saying
plainly what it left and why; a Fable package is trusted with the design, not fenced to a
list. The Opus packages that build out behind a Fable baseline run as a wave when their
baseline is in, as **sibling cloud sessions** rather than subagents of the lead's machine
(each in its own container, so the suites do not share one machine's load; each pushing its
own branch named for its package, `claude/pkg-<n>`, with the owner's permission given at
that wave (**and granted for every builder, Fable or Opus, on 2026-10-27**, after package
73's first run was lost with the machine's rebuild: a builder pushes its worktree branch to
`claude/pkg-<n>` after each commit as a safety net, never force-pushed, nothing merging from
it without the lead's review); the lead fetching, reviewing and merging as now, and running one whole suite on
the merged tree). The lead's own work (the six-on-six measure, the gate document, the
merges, the records, the short plays) is no package. **The suites, from 2026-10-28:** a
builder runs the fast tier once on its final tree and the slow tier of the files it touched,
and after a mend reruns only the mended test's file (and the pace tests when the mend
touches a per-tick path), never a whole tier again; **the whole suite on the merged tree is
the lead's, run in the cloud by the whole-suite workflow** (`.github/workflows/
whole-suite.yml`: the slow tier in six shards, the pace tests alone after, some twenty
minutes) at every merge, so that no builder spends seventy minutes of the shared machine
watching dots (the owner's word). The usage may run to the week's limit
on these packages; that is the owner's choice.

You still have the ruling authority on design decisions and the merge of any work, and I encourage you to stay connected with their work as much as you see fit. If, after some time with this arrangement, we find it less satisfactory (both of us together, not just by my judgement), we can always return to the original setup with you managing every chart package directly." So: the chart session stays on Opus; the lead rules design and merges every chart hash after reading it and after the whole suite in the cloud; the session's own rulings (a block's step 0, a brief's corrections) come to the lead in a line each and are recorded; and the arrangement is looked at again by the owner and the lead together, with the lead managing every chart package directly as the way back.

**After the cold review: close out, and hold (the owner, 2026-11-14, on his first reading of `docs/reviews/ColdReview-M7.md`):** "I've done an initial read of the review, I think that it basically matches my inclination to slow down and take stock of the basics again. I would like to close out what work is in flight, and we don't need to cut anything off immediately, but we should hold writing or starting any new packages for now besides the mend package recommended by the reviewer while we make sure we're both fully about exactly how to best continue. I agree with the proposed order of 96, then 103b after a gate, and 92 last for the reviews." So: the packages in flight are finished as briefed and closed (111; 112; 106b; 60; 103a; the chart session's two mending steps, the tracks' depth and the depth read along a line; the ships session's mends and its Phase 5 to one hash, and package 75's close-out); **nothing new is written or begun** (77, 90's preliminaries, 78a, 78b, 80, 87, 91, 107, 108, 99, 110's builds, M7c all stay held); the one exception is the review's first step, briefed below as package 115 for his approval; and the reviews follow in the review's order: 96 (amended to begin with a first game), then a gate, then 103b, and 92 last.

**How the work goes on: the owner's answers on the procedure (2026-11-14, after the cold review).** The owner, first: "we've been running packages of the same shape on work that has progressively become more complex and less grounded in a principled and cohesively designed basis, but each package still returns something that is considered 'complete', where it generally has become more like 'sufficient to the brief' ... As we've moved from implementing to the written proposal to 'designing on the go', we probably need to make sure that our procedure is still both faithful to the intent and being enacted in the best way for the design, and not just for the completion of packages." The lead put six points to him; his answers, in his words:
1. (A design statement before a brief.) "Agreed, concise and clear design statements are good, and I think what we had this when we were moving in milestones, but as we've stayed in and grown milestone 7, we lost this in the procedure. What we can perhaps do is to either close out the original proposal and create a new one, with a fresh and clear milestone plan to work within again that is sized to be completable and gateable."
2. (Acceptance by a cold player's script.) "This is good in theory, but the game remains centrally built to my personal standard, with the cold player being the secondary ideal still, and I am comfortable with this. It is not a commercial product. I think our gate system before sufficed to cover my experience of each feature, however, as the features grow more complex and multi-faceted, we may need to use more frequent gates, or small-scoped milestones to enable real testing of each feature."
3. (His eye at two points.) "This is covered too, I think, by returning to the true milestone-paced development, rather than a change on your end. I shall apply my close eye manually, so to speak."
4. (Fewer things in flight.) "Yes. Agreed, generally, it will be easier for my mental load and probably for yours. We can still run more than one thing at a time, but it must be done reasonably and within the return to a design reference."
5. (A proposal that is true again.) "Yes. Agreed."
6. (The lead's reports.) "Fair, I think that your reports remain useful, and mostly are only hampered by their frequency between my current ability to keep track of everything in flight versus the design."
His addendum to the first, the same hour: "...that is sized to be completable and gateable, or to at least close out milestone 7 and consider the addition of a new set of milestones sized to be completeable and with gates pre-defined and held to."
So the standard the game is built to is the owner's own, by his own play at a gate; the remedy is the milestone's pace again (a design reference, milestones sized to be finished and gated, gates more often as features grow), not a new layer of procedure. **Not yet settled, and nothing is begun on it:** whether the proposal is closed out and a new one written, or milestone 7 is closed out and a new set of milestones added to the proposal as it stands; either way the milestones are sized to be finished and their gates are written before the work and held to.

**Mends for the cause, not the symptom (the owner, 2026-11-14, on the faults the independent readings have been finding):** "We may be finding more faults recently that likely would have been found in testing for edge cases, so as long as we make sure to plan our fixes for them so as to build for generality rather than fixing the symptom, so to speak, I am alright with this." So, for every mend ruled from a reading: the builder names the fault's general cause (state gone stale across a sleep and a wake; a plan read where the ship's own state should be; a check that samples too coarsely; work paused and begun again as if new), mends it where the cause lives so that every reader of the same thing is served, says in the report where else the same cause was looked for and what was found, and adds the test at that level and not only for the case that was caught. A reader of a mended hash is asked which it is, the cause's mend or the symptom's. The lead's rulings say the cause where he can see it.

**The builders' set-up (the owner, 2026-11-13, evening: "yes, please build it").** Two builders had found their containers without part of the test set-up (package 60: the Playwright package, so every browser plan skipped; package 106a: the server's websocket library, so every browser plan timed out and was taken for the machine's fault). The cloud environment the sessions run in now carries a setup script, by the owner's approval, that installs the project with its `dev` and `server` extras wherever a FreeSail checkout is present and does nothing otherwise (`python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev,server]"`, the line the cloud workflow itself runs; a failed install is said and does not stop the session). It runs when a container is built fresh, so it is unproven until the next new session starts; a session already running runs that one line itself. A builder's report still says that the browser plans played with none skipped.

**Trial merges in the cloud (the owner, 2026-11-13):** "You may use a scratch branch for trial merges, and multiple cloud runs at a time. I trust that you would verify the integrity of this method, as you are directly managing the merging/pushes and repository." **The method, as the lead keeps it:** one scratch branch, `claude/trial`, written by the lead alone and never merged anywhere; a trial is a commit whose tree is exactly the lead's staged trial merge (the trunk's head with the builder's reported hash merged, the two end-of-file appends kept both) and whose parents are the branch's old tip, that base and that hash, so that every push is a fast-forward and none is forced (`trialpush.sh` in the lead's scratch folder). The whole suite is dispatched on it and the run's own `head_sha` is checked against that commit. **A step merges on the trunk only by the builder's hash, and only where the trunk's tree after the merge equals the tree the green run tested** in every file but the lead's own documents; where the trunk has moved by another merge since, the trial is made again on the new head (or made on top of the other trial, so that the pair is tested as it will stand) and never assumed. The lead's own fast tier runs beside it on another step; the run on the trunk after each merge stays. No run on the scratch branch is recorded as the trunk's. **A correction to every run recorded as "green whole" up to run 77 (the lead, 2026-11-13):** the cloud's runners had no browser, so the fourteen browser plans, the pictures' test and the truths that read a page were skipped there in every run, and ran only on the builders' machines and the lead's where someone ran them; run 77 was green on a tree where the letter's plan failed. From run 81 the workflow has a job that installs a browser and plays the plans, failing if one is skipped; the pictures and the pixel truths remain the build machines' to run, their pins being the pre-installed browser's. **Run 81 (2026-11-13, 05:45 to 07:09 UTC, on 477aee7e, the trunk with packages 102's step 3, 109's step 1 and its plan's mend, 110's note and 111's step 1): green in lint, the six shards, the browser plans (the first run to play them: five minutes, none skipped) and the pace job.**

No legacy mode is kept to preserve a fault. What does not change: a save or a pin that moves **by accident** is a fault to find; no test is skipped, disabled or weakened to get a green run; and a builder who finds a save or a pin must move says so and stops for the lead's word unless the brief already gave it.

The Atlantic's road south to the Cape Verde Islands waits behind the same pause.

**An open design question, recorded for the owner (2026-11-10): the day and the range.** The
game's purpose is a world that can be simulated over a wide range of dates, 1792 to 1825 as
it stands, and earlier and later where possible; the build's attention has gathered on 1805
(the scenarios' year, the lights and shores "as 1805 had them", the signal books of 1799 and
1803). The owner's questions, open: which is better, fidelity to the day in every element
or a world that functions reasonably on any given day; and where attention to historical
fidelity gets in the way of an interesting simulation and game, "not because it is not
important to the intent of the game, but because the world must be subject to the game and
not vice-versa". **The owner's ruling the same day (decision 66, `docs/DesignProposal.md`): history is the starting state, not a rail; the elements are correct, their interactions are the world's own once play begins; fidelity is a lever.** How far each element is dated across the range is still open. What the lead notes for the discussion: the data that
carries its dates in its rows (79a's regimes, a port that changes hands by `since` and
`until`, a nation's wars) already answers for any day, while the data written as one year's
picture (a harbour's moles, a coast's lights, a signal book, a ship list) answers for 1805
and is silently wrong elsewhere; so a brief that says "as 1805 had it" builds the second
kind, and briefs from here say which kind each item is.

**A first case found (package 101's builder, 2026-11-10):** the wars of `data/nations.yaml`
carry `since` and no `until`, and `Nations.at_war` reads no date: Britain and Spain are at war
on any day, so the allies of 1808 to 1814 are enemies and a Spanish port refuses a King's ship
in 1809. A port's dated `nation:` (79a's form) does answer for the day. Nothing is changed:
how a dated war is read, as the state on the day a game begins or against the running clock,
is the open half of decision 66 and package 103's ground.

**The discussion so far (the owner and the lead, 2026-11-10; nothing below is ruled beyond
decision 66).** *Three layers*, which the owner likes: the elements (a ship, a gun, a coast, a
wind), held to the record; the state on the day a game begins (who is at war, who holds a
port, which book is in force), the dated seed; and what happened afterwards, which decision 66
frees: the record of it an almanac for the director and the scenario's author to use, bend or
leave, never applied by the engine of itself. *The lever as codified modes*, which matches the
owner's thought: seeded (correct at the start, free afterwards), strict (the record applied,
to see and take some part in a historical scenario), loose (elements allowed out of their
date). **The owner's caution on strict:** the player's own acts may break a scenario in which
no change is allowed, "or at least this will cause some conflict for a strict ruling"; it
needs attention. *The line still to be drawn* (the owner): between "period features" such as
the Barbary states' conflicts, the shifting political, diplomatic and governmental realities
as they bear on the game, and the general features that can happen at any time by
circumstance. *The sources* (the owner): enough on the era at large should be found by further
searches, and by an analysis of the project's own research on file "with an eye to bridging
extant gaps on a reasonable basis for our game and simulation". The lead's thoughts given in
answer, for the record: strict cannot mean that nothing changes, since the player acts; it can
mean that the record proceeds wherever the game has not contradicted it, each recorded event
carrying its conditions in the world's terms (who holds the place, whether the squadron
exists) and happening only if they hold, so that the game's facts outrank the almanac. And a
test for the line: a thing true by circumstance alone is general and has no date; a thing true
over a span of years whatever the player does is a period feature, a dated row; a change at a
moment is an event, the almanac's. The owner's own example divides by it: the corsairs
cruising is a period feature, a bombardment of Algiers an event.

### The owner's testing week: loose ends mended by the lead (2026-10-31 onward)

**The followed hull's log at the drivers (2026-10-31).** The owner, testing 82's visit by
boat, saw nothing of his order in the log, neither refusal nor acceptance. Reproduced at
the console: `send the boat to the Raven with Mr Pearce` works from the prompt (the launch
away, the person aboard her in twenty-five minutes, `where am I` "aboard the Raven, on the
quarterdeck, a visitor, of the Amazon"), but after `follow "Raven"` every order and query
went to her hull and its lines to her log while the console went on listening to the hull it
was attached to at the start (`World.log` is the followed hull's by `_PER_SHIP_FIELDS`, the
listener was on the object), so an order, a refusal or an answer printed nothing; the
browser's driver the same. Mended in both (`Console._follow_log`, `Driver._follow_log`: the
listener moves to the followed hull's log after each line, each tick and each `follow`, so
`go to the boat` and `come alongside` move it too), tests beside each
(`tests/test_console.py`, `tests/test_server.py`); the console, server and observer suites
green here; the whole suite in the cloud on the push (run 29 on `a7440f0`: lint green, 6,264
passed over the six shards, 11 skipped, 10 expected failures, none failed, 41 minutes; the pace
job, informative, 7 of 11, the same four truths under the floor as on runs 24 to 27 on a slow
runner, the matter recorded under 88). Found on the way, for the week's turn:
the player's own body goes aboard another ship only as a person sent in the boat (the
captain's, from the prompt: `send the boat to the Raven with Captain Bowen`, after which
`where am I` answers as a visitor's while the prompt and the readings stay his own ship's
until `follow "Raven"`), or by `--seat captain --ship <name>` at the start; from his own
manned boat (`go to the launch`, `pull for the Raven`) there is no order to go aboard her
(`come alongside` is to his own ship): booked as 82's first follow-up.

**The owner's notes of 2026-11-01 (four points, from the saves `indefatigable-and-schooner-test-2`,
`m7-indefatigable-and-raven-mid-channel` and `boat-between-ships-test`; the lead's reading
against the code, nothing built):**

1. *Says and hails from the other vessel's models not shown to the player, even at the same
   place ashore.* Confirmed in the code: a station's `say` (`orders/stations.py` `_say`)
   delivers the word to `_stations_held(world)`, the speaker's own hull's stations and the
   player's seat there, although 66 and 84 gave `hearing.stations_everywhere` and
   `people_hearing` for every hull; and the line is written in the speaker's hull's log alone,
   which the player's console and browser never show. **For 65** (steps 2 and 4, after the
   reset): the hearers of a word are every hull's stations within hearing (`within_hearing`
   across hulls: ashore at the same place of the same port, aboard the same hull for a
   visitor, a hail within hail between hulls), the word written as heard into each hearing
   hull's log (so the player's log carries what his people heard and the replay stays a
   function of the inputs), and the drivers show it; truth 7-389 (free) takes it.
2. *The player not clearly bound to a single person; travel between ships and `follow`
   unintuitive.* Part of it was the followed-hull log bug, mended at a7440f0. The rest is
   decision 59's spirit carried through: **for 65's step 4**, the player is one person (his
   ship's captain by default, or the seat's person), the prompt and the play log are that
   person's (what reaches him where he is), he moves between ships as a person moves (in the
   boat, the prompt following his body), and `follow` is the owner's eye, a driver's command
   for observing and never the player's road; the primer's chapters 14, 19 and 26 and the
   browser's page say so in one sentence. The missing road, the player going aboard another
   ship from his own manned boat (`go to the launch`, `pull for the Raven`, then aboard her),
   is 82's first follow-up and is taken with step 4. Put to the owner as decision 62.
3. *The browser's play log and prompt as a single person's.* The same: 65's step 4.
4. *A model's station not retained when its person moved ship (a new station "the Mr Hill"
   made and a separate model seated).* On the trunk the harness does move with the person:
   probed here with a fake at the Raven's officer's station sent aboard the Amazon by her
   captain's `send the boat to the Amazon with Mr Newton`: the same harness, model and door
   stood at the visitor's station on the Amazon, the Raven's station emptied. What breaks is
   the agent API's desk (`agents/remote.py`), whose seats are keyed by station name and ship:
   the moved station reads as "mr newton of the Amazon", the remote client's seat loses its
   harness, the new station reads as unseated, and a fresh model is seated at it (the
   director's seats or the door). Two things **for 82's follow-up, not 65**: the desk's seat
   follows the harness (keyed by the harness, not the name and the ship), and the visitor
   keeps his own station's name as the primer's chapter 26 promises ("officer of the watch,
   of the Raven, aboard the Amazon"), not a station named for the man.
   **The owner's account, 2026-11-01 (the API door):** the moment Mr Hill came aboard, the
   Opus door that held the owner's own officer became "the Mr Hill" in its same session (and
   said so), and `stand down the Mr Hill` stood down both him and the officer: the desk had
   the one door covering both stations, the newest by recency. So the desk resolves a door's
   station by recency and not by a seat of its own; the follow-up keys each door to its
   harness.
5. *The glass and making out a sail are unwieldy* (the owner, 2026-11-01): `the glass on`
   and `make out` give the nearest sail, or at best the nearest of the named kind, and the
   wanted sail is hard to name. The rule to build (a loose end for the week's turn, the
   lookout's words in `api/queries.py` and the sail-naming of `world/hail.py`): the most

   mile"), each narrowing the pool; where ambiguity remains, the closer; a name once known

   glass on`, `bearing of` and `pull for`, so that one way of naming a sail serves everywhere.

**The wakes in the fully crewed brig (the owner's point of 2026-11-05, which strengthens 65):**
in four hours and a half the officer of the watch was woken 130 times (28 an hour), the
master 68, the captain 60, the director 24, the lookout 16. The officer's wakes: 27 by a
word from the captain (most of them told to him, rightly), the rest by his own stand-by
conditions, which he set wide ("the deck given, or a message, or a wind shift, or a sail
made out, or ..."); the captain's 60: 38 by "a word from the captain", which were the
master's and the officer's words to him (23 and 8) and in seven cases his own last word.
For 65: the reach rule (a wake carries a line he perceived, by his place) is the cure for a
crowded deck, and two mends for step 2, pinned in the code: (a) the wake's reason for a
word addressed to a station is the fixed string `A_WORD` ("a word from the captain",
`agents/harness.py`, package 29's constant from when only the player's captain spoke),
whoever spoke: the reason names the speaker and the kind (a word, a question, from whom);
(b) the owner's observation, borne out by seven of the captain's sixty wakes following his
own last word: a station woken by its own line. `_heard_between` excludes the station's own
actor, so the road is the addressed word (`a.word`, set by `tell`, `say to` and the words
kept for an unheld station, `orders/stations.py` line 954's "kept for whoever takes the
station"): reproduce with a station that tells or says to a station nobody holds, and with
one that names itself, and make a station's own word never its wake. For the briefs (65's step 2 as well): stand by for the few things that matter, and
let the rest come with the next sample.

**For mulling, not for building (the owner, 2026-11-05): the shape of conversation.** In
life speech is not turn-based: a man speaks, acts and listens at once. The lead's take: the
world is already not turn-based (it ticks on between every station's turns, and a reply
may speak, order and stand by in one turn, which is speaking and acting at once); what is
turn-based is the listening, since a word reaches a station only at its next sample or
wake. The costs are the wake policy (every addressed word a wake, every overheard word a
wait: 41's rule, which 65's reach rule refines) and the floor (the pace rule holds the
ship at 1x while a sample is open, so six doors on one deck crawl). Roads worth mulling,
none taken: words within a short span of ship time folded into one sample per hearer
rather than one wake each (a conversation read as a stream at the station's own cadence);
a "while you spoke" fold for the words that arrived during a long turn; and an attention
rule beside the place rule (a man at the braces does not hear the quarterdeck). The gain of
each measured against the fully crewed brig's figures before anything is built.

### The owner's play of 2026-11-09: nine notes and three saves, triaged (the lead)

The owner played the trunk at 7693cad5 on the *Prince de Neufchatel* in the Rade de Brest (three
saves, kept with the lead and read by the game's own loader, never committed) and wrote nine
notes. Each was reproduced before it was ruled on: four investigations run beside the lead (the
viewer driven in a real browser; the prompt driven live ashore and in the cabin; the tide's own
function at seven points; the code read for the two surveys), and the strike save replayed whole.
What each is, and where it goes:

1. **Her guns show through her ports, run in and secured: a defect of the viewer's paint order**
   (package 98). Her guns are placed by rule, a secured muzzle 0.10 m inside her drawn side on
   every ship (her carronades -0.100, the frigate's long 9s -0.100). A gun's figures sort at
   their own middles, the side's strips and the lids at the middle of the whole strip ring, the
   bilge with it (`client/projection.js`, the guns' `sortAt` and the strips'); her steep deadrise
   puts that point 0.56 to 0.70 m inboard, so her whole short carronade paints over her side and
   lid, where on the brig only a muzzle's face does and on the frigate some.
2. **A flag's canton and stars come and go with the bearing: a defect, every nation's** (98).
   Each part of a flag is a polygon sorted at its own middle, so the canton sorts behind the
   stripes over half the circle (the American ensign loses 16 parts over one half and 5 over the
   other; Britain's loses its canton and crosses the same way), against the design's own "a flag
   sorts at its own middle as a sail does" (Design-ViewerAction §12.3). Beside it: a drawing's
   `lines` are not drawn (the saltires), and a flag has no rank among the kinds.
3. **The chart and the ship view tell more than the person knows: confirmed, a design step**
   (package 99). The browser is served the whole snapshot (`api/queries.snapshot`); the knowledge
   rule greys the instruments' readouts alone. Off the deck the views still show the true and
   apparent wind, the heading, the sails, the strangers and what is in sight, and the master's
   account run on live (the chart shows the reckoning, never the true position); ashore or a
   prisoner the same. Nothing keeps "the last value he learned" today.
4. **A cabin view and a view ashore: not now, the lead's advice** (the owner asked to be argued
   with). The ship viewer stays a ship viewer for this milestone. What the person below or
   ashore should see falls out of note 3: the ship as he last saw her, greyed and stamped with
   the hour. A scene for the cabin and for the quay wants things to show (the table, the papers,
   the people, a port's places), which are the career's and the port's content of milestone 8;
   booked there with package 92's building, not as a viewer mode of milestone 7.
5. **A signal ordered from the cabin: no rule says, and the code lets it** (98, for the owner's
   word). The rule as written gives the deck's orders as the sails, the yards, the lines, the
   helm, the anchors and all hands (the primer's chapter 14; spec M7b §14); "beat to quarters"
   and "fire a gun" are refused below too. The colours and the signals are sent to their handler
   before the place is checked (`orders/__init__.py`), so they are done from the cabin, the only
   orders of the deck that are. The lead's advice: they are the deck's, refused below in the
   same words, until a captain can pass the word from his cabin (a later step: "pass the word to
   the officer of the watch: ...", with the minute it takes).
6. **Commands with no answer in the log, ashore and below: the worst of the nine** (98, first).
   Driven live in a browser: of 45 lines typed, 30 showed nothing. The server answers every one;
   the page is sent a line only if the person "hears" it, and the player's own readings
   (`query.*`, classed as said on deck) and refusals (`order.*`, classed as the deck's) are
   dropped whenever he is not on deck (`world/knowledge.hears`), against the design's own "the
   asker's own question, heard where he asked it" (Design-PlaceKnowledge). So ashore and in the
   cabin every reading and every refusal is silent, the console's the same. Beside it, the page
   takes any two-word line beginning "go" as a clock command ("go below", "go ashore", "go
   aloft" never reach the server). **The testing procedure the owner asks for** is prototyped
   (the server launched on a port, a headless browser typing each line, the server's answer, the
   socket's frames and the log's new rows kept side by side, each line marked shown or not): to
   be a kept tool with plans by place and state (98's first step), so that every mend of 98 is
   proven as the player sees it.
7. **The model officer was sent no chart picture: the OpenRouter door never fetches it** (98).
   The `chart` tool is offered and answers "a picture of 1200 by 900 pixels", but that door's
   model is built without the picture's fetch (`agents/api.py`; the first door has it), so the
   image part is never added, for every model at that door, whatever it can read, in every
   place. The words told the model a picture was drawn.
8. **Letters and things as one system: surveyed, a package of its own** (package 100). Today a
   `Thing` has a description and a keeper but no text; "read" and "open" show nothing; nothing
   removes or destroys a thing; a letter is a `Message`, read to the captain on arrival and gone;
   a letter sent ashore by the boat is dropped at the landing; the player can draft a book but
   no letter.
9. **The Goulet's stream over the whole Rade: confirmed, data** (98). The `the-goulet` area is a
   box from 48.29 to 48.37 N and 4.62 to 4.42 W (`data/tides/streams.yaml`), the narrows and most
   of the bay: 4.9 kn at springs at the owner's position and in the middle of the Rade; east and
   north of the box the open Channel's stream answers (1.8 kn towards 245 degrees, "By the
   master's reckoning she is in the open Channel" in the owner's own log). No text in the
   repository gives the Rade's rate; the design's own note points to the hydrographic service's
   atlas of the roads, not yet read.

**The strike save, replayed** (the owner fired on a French frigate under French colours, lost
his captain to a shot, struck and was taken): five defects of package 74's step 3, sent to its
builder to mend with step 4. The captive's own words at the prompt were taken as the player's
hand, so the captor's captain stood aside and she lay aback and took the ground forty-five
minutes on; the captor engaged his own prize a minute after taking her and fired 25 shot into
her; a bare "Yes." was not read for the parole; a prisoner's "hail her" was performed, and the
prize answered "prize to Mr Ray's ship"; "go ashore" was refused in a free man's words. What
worked as designed: the first lieutenant succeeding the dead captain and taken as "the first
lieutenant of", the parole asked in French, the sword, the places, the refusals of the deck.

### Package 60, steps 1 and 2 as reported at ab0ade58: NOT merged; the lead's reading and what is owed (2026-11-13)

The builder's report at ab0ade58 (`claude/pkg-60`): step 1 reconciled with package 109's refusal of "take command" (7a787ff0), the three mends owed from the first reading (b2290253), and step 2, the company moved by the boat (f5252254, `freesail/world/transfer.py`, the order `transfer ... to ...`), with the builder's suites green. It merges clean on the trunk at 18ea2816 with package 109's step 4 under it. An independent reading (a fresh reader given the code and not the lead's view, probing on the builder's own fixtures) found step 2 not ready and one fault in step 1. The three mends (A), (B), (C) are right as far as they go and each has a test that fails without it. **Owed before it is trialled again, most severe first:**

1. **A ship taken up from ordinary stays asleep (step 1; mend (C) is too narrow).** Forty minutes after `take command of her` the Fly is still not awake, in the far shape and not at anchor, her log saying she could not be boxed off: the hulls woken are only those he left, the player's own ship is skipped by `crewed()`, and `take_up` clears the regime without waking her. His own ship then reads as coarse to the dealings, and a lay-up of the ship he left is refused as lying at no anchor. A test that takes up a sleeping ship and finds her awake, at her anchor and workable.
2. **The tail lays up the ship he commands.** `transfer two hands to the Fly, and lay the Sherbourne up`, given aboard the Sherbourne, leaves his own ship in ordinary and worked by one, and nothing takes her out again. Refused in words unless the order also moves him, or the design note says what becomes of a captain whose ship is laid up under him.
3. **Every load deals the receiver's whole muster again.** Two hands coming aboard changed the watch of 26 of the Fly's 40; men at work lost their place and were taken by another evolution; the quarter bill is dropped and the battery set to hold. The hands who come are added to the watches as they stand (the smaller watch first), nobody already aboard is moved, and the giver loses only those who go: as the prize crew's taking out already does on a working ship.
4. **A lost boat is used and comes back whole.** No check of the boat lost, as the dealings make; a boat "lost: swamped" ended "at the booms".
5. **The same men in two musters.** With one ship's second load for another still on her books, a second transfer alongside draws those men again and sends her boat home; they later join both. A man told off for a load is out of the giver's count from the order.
6. **Persons are put aboard before they are rehomed,** the reverse of the prizes' order, so an officer held by a seated party arrives as a visitor; and the officer a ship was left to (`command_passed_to`) can be moved out of her.
7. **Loads are never checked again.** They arrive at their ticks if either ship has sailed off; where the receiver is gone nothing is said in any log; the list of hulls left is never pruned.

**One road, not two (the owner's standing concern, a feature built beside one that exists).** The dealings already carry persons between hulls by the boat (`Dealings.send_boat_to`, `_boat_to_job`, `BoatState.people` and `landing`, the boat's own pace and refusals). The transfer keeps its own list, timing and refusals. It goes by the existing road, or the notes say in a paragraph what that road cannot carry and the lead rules. The same for the draw of hands (`prizes._draw_prize_crew`, to be shared and not copied), the joining of names (`dealings._and`), the check of way on her (`boats.man_boat`'s) and the ships given (`command.given_to`).

**Words that are not the world's.** "no ship of the player's in this world", "wants a ship in a world", "at the prompt", "this world is observed ('ship: none')", "has no hull of her own yet"; refusals that name the Amazon or the Fly whatever ships exist; a berth count said in figures beside one in words.

**Tests that cannot fail or are missing.** The keepers' path never runs in its test (29 against room for 15: only the berth refusal is reached); a third refusal's reason is unpinned and its "nothing changed" cannot fail; one assertion is always true; the only save test is slow (a fast one is wanted: saved with a load in the boat, loaded, the load arriving). Untested: alongside, `from X`, the lay-up tail, the receiver gone, a transfer between two King's ships (the builder's own note), and the refusals for way on her, beyond the pull, a prisoner, an observed world and a ship not his.

The readers' probe scripts are kept with the lead and are the lead's to pass on request. Step 1 is not merged apart from step 2: its fault (1) is its own, and the two share the files.

The owner, the same evening: "I would just like to be able to get out from under the work that is currently in flight, which feels a bit interminable at this point, so that I can actually understand and follow what is happening as it happens, rather than being behind it all as I am now." And earlier: "I would like to get to wrapping up what is in flight without too much more finagling."

So, for the six things in flight (package 75; package 103a; package 60; package 115 parts A and B; package 115 part D; the chart session's tracks step), and for nothing else:

If it is sound it goes to the cloud and merges. If it wants a builder again, it is PARKED on its branch with its list, unmerged, and the owner is told; no further round is sent without his word.

### The owner's words of 2026-11-14, night, and what follows from them (the lead)

Four things the owner said that evening, kept here in his words because they govern the close-out and the work after it:

- "My primary desire now is to ensure we still have a functional game to the standard it was on the last version I played, as I really don't have a good sense of what has been built since then, functionally, and what has changed at a core level." The version he last played is the trunk at 746c0bb7 (11 November): his saves of 12 November carry its rules' stamp exactly. On the trunk since then the game's own code changed little (more sea, the mends from his play, the signals drawn, the ports' dated rows, the chart's corrections); the changes at the core were all in the six things in flight.
- "Generally speaking, I am not attached to my playtest saves for the purpose of development. If a change invalidates an old save, or an old scenario, that is not necessarily a fault if the shape of the game is changing in the new version such that the old save reasonably can't play on the new version. I think this will have to be the case as the game evolves through development, and the essence of the game is not in any of the currently existing scenarios necessarily." So a replay of his saves is a diagnostic and never a gate.
- "Oh, and you have my permission to parallelize the cloud runs however necessary to more efficiently run the suites and merges." From this the scratch branches `claude/trial-2` to `claude/trial-6`, one run of the whole suite on each, beside `claude/trial`.
- "I think everything is generally fine, and the code is likely stable. We'll just need to move back to more constrained and pre-registered scope to get back to the pace that works for me, and allows us to more carefully and fully design features and packages rather than reacting to them." This heads the continuation: `docs/dev/ContinuationProposal.md`, which he asked for the same night ("You may consolidate a continuation proposal for once everything currently in flight is parked/merged based on the cold review and the current state").

**How the six were tried.** As a chain, each link one package merged on the last, each link's tree run whole on its own scratch branch: the trunk with 103a; then 75; then 60; then 115 part D; then 115 parts A and B; then the chart session's tracks step. A link merges when its own run and every run before it is green and its builder has reported that hash; the merge on the trunk reproduces the link's tested tree exactly (checked by a diff).

**A slip of the lead's, mended.** When the session's disk filled during this work, a merge of the tracks step meant for a scratch checkout ran in the trunk's own checkout and stood there uncommitted for some minutes. It was aborted; nothing was committed or pushed.

### Package 115, part C (the director's limits), as merged (2026-11-16)

**Merged at 9649ff25 by the reported hash f42231f6** (ten commits on the trunk at eabdd40c; ten files, all within card 4 of `docs/dev/ScopeCards-BeforeTheGate.md` and the leave the lead gave at the ground report). The tree is the tree of the cloud's run 128 (every required job green; the informative pace job is spoken of below), and differs from it in nothing. Built by a builder of the Fable tier; read three times by independent readers of the Opus tier, once at each hash it offered.

**What a director and a player have from it.**
- **The director is free by default, as the owner ruled,** the player's own ship, person and prompt included: her intent by any spelling, a thing found or made aboard her, a wound, a strike or a prize, `follow`. Nothing refuses the director for being the director (truth 7-462).
- **A brief's limits hold by every spelling,** because they are judged on what the order is and not on its words. There is one table of the director's order forms (`freesail/world/orders.py`, `WORLD_ORDER_FORMS`: forty-three forms, each with whom it reaches and whether it can kill). Every handler of the channel says what it is about to do once its names are resolved and before anything changes; `orders.judged(world, order)` runs it to that point; the channel, the brief's limits, the doubt and the log all read that one judgement. The door and its dry run share one sequence. Under a brief that sets a limit, an order the judgement cannot read is not handed on.
- **One limit a brief may newly set, and no shipped brief sets: `hands_off_the_players_ship: true`.** It refuses every order judged to reach his ship (the ship his prompt is aboard), his person or his prompt, `say as` one of her people among them. What comes from outside is not refused: the weather, a sail, a letter, a port, a mark, a person or thing ashore that is not hers.
- **`nobody_dies` has something to refuse:** the grave wound, and a boat lost while anyone is in her. The owner settled its reach on 16 November: "Agreed on your ruling for 'nobody dies' refusing acts that directly kill. For the case of a director, such an order can only reasonably restrain actual direct killing actions, as the consequence of various other actions can't be properly guaranteed to such a standard." So a hazard the ship can answer (a fire, a leak, a gale, an enemy) is not refused by it; the brief's own words now say so.
- **`enemy_heaviest` is asked wherever a ship comes to be an enemy's:** made, as a convoy's escort, by commissioning, struck to or made a prize of an enemy's ship, or a prize the court restores to an enemy. A weight the limit cannot rank ("a line-of-battle ship", "a 74") is refused, not passed.
- **`wind_max_kn` is judged by the weather's own functions with every system standing,** not by the ordered system's own bell: on copies of the systems, at the ordered system's rings (half a radius to two radii, sixteen bearings), every other system's centre and the ship, at twenty-five times from the order to the end of the system's track or of its growing in, four days at the most. An order is refused if any reading it raises, by so little as a hundredth of a knot, stands over the brief's figure; so several lows each mild alone are not stacked into a gale. **What it does not read, and why that is left:** weather ordered to come later than the readings end, and a field that moves on after them. The second reader got a low ordered twelve days ahead past quiet-passage's 27 knots (judged 20.7; it would blow 55.5), and a chain of waypoints past the fourth day to 63.5. The lead ruled a mend (the whole four days always read; weather ordered further ahead refused under a wind limit); the owner, on reading it, set the standard instead: "For the wind, we needn't overengineer it, as the director, given a wind limit, tries earnestly as far as I have seen to follow it, and so at a certain point, we can assume at least a reasonable good intent from the director as far as not exceeding the wind limit." The ruling was withdrawn before any of it was built. The wind's limit is a guard against an earnest director's mistake; beyond what it reads it rests on the director's good faith, and the primer and the tuning notes say so.
- **The director's log says whom each act reached** ("; it reached the player's own ship (the Amazon)"), `follow` included. No line is said to the player, as the owner ruled.
- **An order carries one `[reason: ...]`, at its end.** A second, or one in the middle, is refused in words.
- A crash is gone: `ship "<the player's ship>": in ordinary` raised an error out of the director's door; it is refused in the game's words.

**What moved, old beside new** (at length in `docs/dev/TuningNotes.md`, the package's section at the end).
- **Truth 7b-90's directed day.** The fake director's "soft low" was 1006 hPa and was done under quiet-passage's 27 knots, because the old limit read only the low's own bell: 11.4 knots. Measured by the weather's own functions that low blew **28.5 knots** at its hardest with the field standing: a real breach of the brief, which the old estimate under-read. It is now 1010 hPa: **24.8 knots** at its hardest, and done. The field alone never stands over 21.0 knots within the judged reach during the low's track, so the stricter rule does not stop quiet-passage's director making weather. The truth's assertions are as written. Found by the lead's own slow run, not by the builder (whose note that no test's figure moved was wrong in the slow tier); measured by the builder; passed by the lead and by the second reader.
- **The forms' examples test and truth 7-367,** which calls it: the test's near sea gained a French lugger made a prize, so that the new form `port.court` has an example the test performs. Assertions unchanged. `aboard the Harpy: a cask found stove` is doubted there now (one form, one doubt, whatever hull), which the test already accepted.
- **Words only, no pin:** `nobody_dies` in a brief's limits ("nobody dies: nothing found aboard that would kill" became "nobody dies by your hand: no act that kills of itself (a grave wound, a boat lost with anyone in her); a hazard the ship can answer ... is not refused by it"); the wind's refusal now says it was reckoned with every system standing.
- **No pinned world digest moved.** The checkpoint's names list is not regenerated: nothing new can be held in a checkpoint (the first hash had a record class that could; the cloud's run 125 caught it, truth 7-606; it is now a plain tuple).
- **A save from before the package, replayed,** no longer performs a director's order with two reason brackets, nor one the limits now refuse. Accepted under the owner's standing word on older saves.

**For the owner: what each shipped brief now refuses that it let through.** All six starters set the same five limits and differ in two figures: quiet-passage (27 knots, a cutter), interesting-passage (33, a brig), chase (33, a brig), dispatches (30, a brig), captive (40, a frigate), hard-cruise (47, a frigate); each sets `nobody_dies`, the war as it is and the chart as it is. None sets hands-off or forbids false colours. Each now refuses: a person badly hurt, by any spelling; the boat lost while anyone is in her; an enemy named by a weight it cannot rank; an enemy heavier than its limit brought in as a convoy's escort, by commissioning, by a strike or prize to an enemy's ship, or by a court's restoring (so, under a starter brief, the player's own ship ordered to strike to an enemy is refused where she is heavier than the brief's limit: she would be an enemy's); a weather system that raises the wind over its figure anywhere in its reach, within the time read, with the field standing; an order with two reason brackets. "The chart as it is" refuses nothing, since no form changes the chart. **No shipped brief's limits were changed;** whether any should be is his to say.

**How it ran, and the lead's errors of process, which are the lead's.**
- **The ground report first** (no code): which tests have a director in them (108 in 23 files; no pinned digest belongs to a directed passage), and that no word a model is shown at the director's station enters the consent question's re-asking (the game compares the consent brief's own sections alone; a test holds it). The lead ruled five questions and gave leave for four small things outside the card's list of files (the `harm` of four entries of `data/director/aboard.yaml`; one false sentence each of the tool's description and of `docs/agents/Harness.md` section 19).
- **Four passes.** The first hash (2d8a4e37) was read by the lead's independent reader, who found five things to mend: two reason brackets passed every limit, the doubt and the log; a heavy friend struck to an enemy became an enemy never weighed; hands-off refused acts on the world's own people ashore; **the truth numbers the lead had given were partly taken** (7-420 to 7-429, by packages 65 and 76: the lead's fault; they are 7-462 to 7-469); and the wind was judged one system at a time, so four lows of 26.6 knots each stood together at 117. The mend closed them; the lead then found the mended wind's one-knot threshold left a stack by small steps, and it became a hundredth of a knot. The hash then reported (157095a) was read again by a second independent reader, who found the five closed, broke the mend five ways and saw the tests catch each, ran every example of the forty-three forms dry and entered with nothing raised, and ran 123 orders before and after under the free brief with only the three declared changes; and who found two things: the wind walked round through time (above: left, by the owner's word) and **a prize court's `restores` putting a struck enemy back on the sea unweighed**, which the last pass mended, with the court's word spelled ("restors"). The last hash (f42231f6: four files, some sixty lines, the wind's judgement byte for byte as it was) was read by a third reader, held to the owner's standard (an earnest director's mistake, not an adversary): nothing to mend; the restoring refused for a heavy enemy prize and done for a neutral's, a retaken British ship and an enemy prize within the limit; `condemns` untouched; the new test fails with the mend taken out; no court order raises.
- **The cloud ran four times:** run 125 on the first hash (three red: the checkpoint's names, and the new form's example not performed in two tests); run 126 on a mend pushed and not yet reported (three red: truth 7b-90, and two tests of the channel the mend had broken); run 127 on the hash reported at the second pass (157095a): the eight required jobs green; the ninth, the pace tests (run alone and informative), red on two of fifteen (the gate's day with the region loaded at 491 ticks a second and truth 7-159's convoy of six at 467, against a floor of 500). **That was the runner and not the package, by measure and not by inference:** the pace job took 514 seconds where run 126's, on all but the last small mends of the same code, took 445 and passed; and a thousand ticks of each of the two worlds make exactly the same number of calls on the trunk and on the merged tree (12,928,669 for the convoy, 11,528,602 for the region), with one call into the files the package changed, the same on both. The two floors sit close to what a slow runner gives; that is for the cheaper-suite work and not this package. Run 128 on the last hash (f42231f6): the eight required jobs green; the pace job, which runs after them and gates nothing, had not ended when the merge was made.
- **The lead's errors.** (0) Against the wind the lead three times ruled a harder wall than the game needs (the field's own functions was right; the hundredth of a knot and then the four days' refusal were the lead building against an adversary where the owner's standard is an earnest director): readers are now told which standard to hold before they attack. (1) The builder said at the ground report that the fast tier had not finished in fifty minutes; the lead took that for a limit of the container and agreed a narrower set of tests. It was the builder's own time limit, as the owner saw in its session and said. With a limit of three hours the builder ran the fast tier whole: 8,255 passed, none failed, in 93 minutes on four workers (and 8,256 in 85 minutes at the last hash). (2) The lead told the owner that two new reds "got through because it ran only the director's files": an inference given as a fact. Both files were inside its set; they broke on a hash it had pushed and not yet reported, with its own gate still running. (3) Twice the lead took a pushed, unreported hash and sent findings piecemeal, five messages where the rule is one list. **The rules that came of it, owner-amended that day and written in the scope cards' file:** the lead gates the hash a builder has reported, never one it has merely pushed; a builder runs the fast tier whole with a limit of hours; a time limit a builder set itself is not a limit of its container, and the lead asks which; a package may take a few passes, each one gathered list.

**Found and not mended (listed, not built).**
- `two stories` shows the director's log with no reveal recorded and the director not told. The owner's to say.
- The acts that kill only at a remove are listed in the tuning notes for the record; by the owner's word they are not refused, and nothing is pending on them.
- `false_colours: false` is still judged on the words of the order. No shipped brief sets it.
- The rules captain of another hull is said to be held by "the player at the prompt", so the rule of reach refuses `say as` him (older).
- The squadrons' literal `the ship` is the game's first hull; after the player takes command of another ship it means the one he left (older; the judgement reads it as the squadron's code performs it).
- After `take up`, the player's new ship is not found by `ship "<her name>": ...`; the order ends in words (older).
- Each dry run copies the world: two to five seconds.
- `health.hit` may tell a station of a grave wound for a light hurt (older; not looked into).
- A seeded system the world draws later can stack on a director's low after the fact; no order makes it, so nothing judges it.
- The director's sentence of a court is performed on a prize still at sea, bound for the port, and at any port's court (older, package 74's).
- A heavy enemy prize retaken by her own side is already an enemy's and on the sea; the court's restoring of her is refused for her weight under a starter brief, though it puts no new enemy there. Rare; the third reader's.
- The court is named two ways for one sentence (the record says the High Court of Admiralty, the order's words the Vice-Admiralty court at the port): older.
- How the restoring weighs a prize held as a far record and not a hull at sea was not tried.
- Real text that holds "[reason:" (a letter's words, a speech put in a mouth) is refused in words by the one reading of an order; a bracket written with letters of another alphabet is not read as a reason and the order fails as unreadable. Accepted.
- The cost of a weather order under a wind limit: one to five seconds at the door, four to eight for a dry run (the reader's measure; the notes' first figure was wrong and is corrected).
- A harbour test that reads the page in a browser failed once in the builder's container under load and passed alone; it passed on the cloud.

**For the consent revision (card 2), carried and not changed here.** The consent brief says the director is "later" and "to come". Nothing in it says that a director may act on the ship an instance commands, wound its person, make its ship strike or move its prompt, nor that a player's brief may forbid that.

**How it is tried.** By the owner, as card 4 says: the director's seat from the harbour, an order to the player's ship done under a brief with no limits and refused in words under a brief of his own with `hands_off_the_players_ship: true`, then the director's log. By the lead first, as he asked, as a model at the director's station through the game's own door (`POST /api/agents/director`, the consent question answered, the drill, then `world_order` calls, with `dry_run` to try one; the director's log at `/api/director/log` with the page's mark); the lead's notes of that will be under `docs/playtests/`.

### Package 116 (the four small mends), as merged (2026-11-17)

**Merged at 8dd5f3df by the reported hash 5b9c369f** (eight commits on the trunk at 15dc5784; twenty-six files, all within card 5 of `docs/dev/ScopeCards-BeforeTheGate.md` and the leave the lead gave at the ground report). The tree is the tree of the cloud's run 129 (all nine jobs green, the pace job among them), and differs from it in nothing. Built by a builder of the Fable tier in one pass; read by two readers of the builder's own and by the lead's independent reader of the Opus tier, who found nothing to mend.

**What a player has from it.**
- **The merchant brig lets go her anchor.** The cause was the muster and not the order: letting go wants about a dozen, her ten seamen are mustered seven to starboard and three to larboard (each station's odd hand goes to starboard), and the harbour's scenario begins with the larboard watch on deck, so the three and the master were under half the want and the order waited for ever. Every other small vessel anchored. Letting go the anchor now calls all hands when the watch is too few (`too_few: all hands`, as the settee's work and the boat's already do): in the harbour she calls all hands at once, rides at anchor a minute in and pipes down; she weighs, and `let go the anchor` brings her up again. Her muster is untouched. The harbour's line "at anchor off Falmouth" is true by the mend, and truth 7-627, which had excused the brig by name from the scenarios' opening orders, excuses nobody now.
- **`strike the colours` strikes her colours,** with the fighting orders loaded as without. The cause: the fighting orders hold a standing order named "the colours", and an unquoted name after `strike`, `show`, `belay`, `avast` or `resume` was read as the book's before the order's own reading. One rule now: unquoted words that are a whole order of the vocabulary are the order; quoted, or with "standing order", they are the book's. So `show the colours` shows her colours too, and `strike "the colours"` still strikes the standing order. Of the 315 standing orders' names the game ships only "the colours" is also an order, so nothing else changed its meaning. `strike colours` and `strike her colours` are understood.
- **The wheel shot away stops the helm.** Before, a helm order was accepted, logged as carried out, and she did not answer; manoeuvres began and miscarried. Now the helm orders and the manoeuvres that drive the helm are refused in the ship's words, which say why and what to order ("The wheel is shot away and the helm does not answer: rig the relieving tackles ... or repair the wheel ..."); the sail orders stand, and `heave to` stands, by her sails, and says the helm does not answer. **`rig the relieving tackles`** gives the helm back at **half the wheel's rate** (the owner: "I think that the relieving tackles would surely be a more strenuous and rudimentary control than the proper wheel ... so I support steering being slower by the rigged tackles"; a judgement said as one, Luce 1884 the source that it is slower and not of the figure; measured by the reader at exactly half). **`repair the wheel`** is a repair evolution of its own, the carpenter's crew of four, with or without the tackles rove; when it is done she steers by the wheel at the wheel's rate and the tackles are cast off. A game saved with the wheel lost, with the tackles rove or in the middle of the repair loads and goes on rightly, from its checkpoint and by a replay. There is no way to be left with a ship that can never steer.
- **The game's own captain answers a lost wheel as a seaman would:** he gives no helm order while the wheel is lost and the tackles not rove, rigs the tackles first whatever the wind (that he never did when it blew thirty knots and above was his own rule, mended), and has the wheel repaired in its turn when out of action.
- **The cruiser's prize doctrine is read.** The thirteen keys of `data/captains/cruiser.yaml` are under `thresholds:` where the reader looks, and the same thirteen are in the revenue cutter's file, whose book is the cruiser's. **Nothing sails differently for it:** of the thirteen, seven are read by the code and each has the value the code already fell back to; no recorded passage moved in either tier.

**A correction to the card.** Its "how the owner tries it" says `port your helm`. That is not an order of the game, with the wheel or without (nor `starboard your helm`, `hard a-port`): the example was the lead's and wrong. To try the wheel use `steer ...`, `helm a-lee`, `bear up` or `tack`.

**What moved, old beside new** (reasons in `docs/dev/TuningNotes.md`, "Package 116"). Truth 7-590's count of the audit's mechanical findings, 61 to 60 (the cruiser's finding is no longer made); the audit's data-owned known findings, 29 to 28, its one entry taken out of the known list by hand at the lead's word (that list is kept by hand and checked by its tool; the lead's brief had wrongly called it generated); truth 7-627, the brig no longer excused (a strengthening); the evolutions counted, 109 to 110; the tests' registers of works that call all hands and of works held take the anchor and the wheel's repair, and the tackles move from "nothing makes it false while held" to a tried case (held, the wheel repaired meanwhile, taken up: refused as not wanted). Truth 7-626, the one recorded passage in which a wheel is shot away: no assertion moved; it still tells its story. The checkpoint's names list regenerated by its tool, 329 before and after: the wheel's repair came, and the director's `Form` went (no checkpoint ever held one; package 115 C's note that the entry still resolved was not so). No test was weakened: the lead's reader read every changed line and broke each mend in turn, and the new truths 7-630 to 7-635 each failed.

**How it ran.** A ground report first, run and not guessed (the fast and slow tiers whole with the keys moved), which is how it was known before building that the prize doctrine moves nothing. One build, one reported hash, no list back. The builder's own gate at that hash: the fast tier whole, 8,263 passed and none failed; the slow tier whole, 556 passed and none failed. Three of its whole runs were cut by its container restarting, not by any limit, and each was run again.

**Left for the owner, none of it built.**
- **The brig's watches of seven and three.** On the watch of three, `set the fore topsail` and every job that wants nine or more hands still waits; the anchor's mend does not touch that. Evening her watches to five and five would mend it and re-make two tests whose story was built on seven and three. Asked of him on 16 November; not yet answered.
- **Six keys of the prize doctrine are read by no code,** in any captain's file: `mans_prizes`, `divide_prisoners`, `prisoners_most`, `burns_when`, `worth_least`, `fit_least`. The doctrine is written; what would act on those six is not built.
- `strike the flag`, `port your helm`, `starboard your helm`, `hard a-port`, `haul your wind` are not orders of the game.
- The wheel's repair is given as half an hour and takes thirty-four to forty-five minutes at the crews' rates, by the ship; the primer says half an hour.
- A wheel shot away a second time while the repair is in hand is mended by the one repair.
- While the wheel is lost, a standing order with a helm action (the default book's "keep her full") is refused each time it fires, a line a minute until the tackles are rove. By design; noisy.
- The game's captain may still give `wear ship` in the minutes before his tackles are rove (one refused line in his name), and his `engage her to ...` and `grapple her` are not among the orders he withholds. A far (asleep) hull sails her plan whatever her wheel. The watch's "Kept her away" can be said with the helm not answering.
- The cutter's and the merchant ship's lines on the harbour's shelves were not examined for the same kind of untruth the brig's was suspected of.

**For the consent revision (card 2), listed only.** The primer's chapter 25 now says the tackles steer at half the wheel's speed and names `repair the wheel`; if anything a model is told describes the wheel or the helm, it wants the same words.

### Package 117 (the consent revision), step 1, the code, as merged (2026-11-17)

**Merged at 63e4503c by the reported hash 43c1016c** (nine commits on the trunk at 90581e79; card 2 of `docs/dev/ScopeCards-BeforeTheGate.md`). The tree is the tree of the cloud's run 131 (the eight required jobs green; the informative pace job red on a slow runner, measured as below), and differs from it in nothing. Built on the Opus tier at the owner's word ("I changed 117 to Opus rather than Fable, as it's a fairly simple package overall"), in two passes; read by the builder's own readers and twice by the lead's independent reader. **Nothing under `docs/agents/consent/` and not `docs/agents/ConsentBrief.md` is touched by this step:** the brief's own words are step 2's draft, for the owner's approval, and step 3's applying.

**The ground report, before any code** (the brief read sentence by sentence against the game, twice: by the builder and by a reader of its own). It found five doors, not four (the OpenRouter dialect shares the local runner's code); the token missed in three places; the operator's voice carrying the night orders, the standing orders' names, the last holder's handover note whole, the last twenty lines of the log and, for the director, the player's brief; and **twenty-nine sentences of the consent brief that the game does not bear out**, each with its file and line, which are the list for the revision. And one piece of good news said plainly: no yes on file was given against the brief as it stands today, so every one of the seven identities with a yes is already owed the question once at its next seating, and the revision adds no asking.

**What a model has from the code.**
- **The opt-out token is heard wherever a reply can carry it.** One function (`model.opt_out_in`) reads everything a model sent: its words, every call's name and every argument, nested values included, always all of them; and each door builds what it scans from the model's own output, whole. It is called at every door (the API door, its OpenRouter dialect, the local runner, the MCP bridge, the terminal) and at the game's own desk in every phase: in turn, out of turn, paused, for a reply cut off, and in the consent conversation while the owner has the word (where a reply used to be dropped unread). The hole the cold review named is closed: at the local runner a token in any other field of a call written in the text never reached the scan. **A token after a stand-down is heard too** (older than the package; found by the lead's reader): a model that has stood down and then writes the token, or `opt_out`, or `final`, at a door that still takes its calls, has its leaving kept as its own withdrawal, so that the consent question is put again before it is seated in that game, or it is not seated again. From another identity it is not heard. A test fails if a door is added that builds a reply the list does not know.
- **The operator's voice holds only words the code wrote.** The first four items of a station's brief (the disclosure, the opt-out and the documentation word for word as they were; the authority in the code's own words) and the station brief with the names taken out; then one sentence saying that the situation follows. Everything that comes from the world is the first piece of data after it, "the situation at the seating": the ship, the person's name and outline, his fellows, the voyage, the journal's last note, the captain's word and night orders, the standing orders' names, the director's player's brief, the log's last lines and the readings. The review's own case is a test at every door: a standing order, a person, a ship and a handover note each worded as an operator's instruction reach an officer as data and nowhere in the operator's voice. The visitor's and the passenger's briefs are in line with the rest. Nothing a model learned before is lost; a game saved before the change loads and is taken up rightly.
- **A model's station may not reach into another model's station.** From a model's station `show the journal of <a held station>`, `resume <a station>` and `stand down <a station>` are refused in words; from the human's prompt and the player's own seat they work as before; and where a model captain used to be told to say `resume ...` it is told that a pause is the human's to answer. **This is a ruling of the lead's, on the side of keeping what the brief says** (the stop and the pause are the human's; a journal is its keeper's), told to the owner on 17 November and his to overturn.
- **Promises about leaving kept:** after an opt-out the game is saved whatever road the world came by (a load from a checkpoint, a restore, a station driven in the game's own process); an opt-out and `final` hold across every ship of the game and not one; a captain stood down when a race ends is told the race is over.
- **Words made true:** the watcher is no longer told to say an order it is refused; the director is told that the game holds a brief's limits as far as it can judge them and that they are the director's to keep beyond that (the owner's standard of 16 November); the sentence that says what the situation holds says "what of these the station has".

**What moved, old beside new** (`docs/dev/TuningNotes.md`, "Package 117"). Truth 46, that the brief's head carries five items in order, is superseded by design: four items in the operator's voice and the situation as the first data, an honest statement of the new shape and at least as strict (the lead's reader). The tests that read the brief at its old place read it where it is now, the same property each (fourteen files; none weakened); the handover's budget in one test, 23,000 to 23,500 characters, the situation being counted where it is kept. No world's digest and no recorded passage moved. The three fixed items are byte for byte the trunk's at six stations.

**How it ran.** A ground report; the lead's word; a first reported hash (cfabbdfa: the fast tier whole 8,348 passed, the slow tier of thirty-five files with the truths whole); the cloud's run 130 on it, the eight required jobs green; the lead's reader, strict on the token alone, who found two things to mend and one older hole the lead put in under that one strict standard; a second pass (43c1016c: the fast tier whole 8,355 passed, the slow tier 1,507 passed); the cloud's run 131 and a short reading of the delta. The second reading, strict on the token after a release and ordinary elsewhere, found nothing to mend in the visitor's and passenger's briefs, the words about a paused station, the small words or the saver, broke the mend two ways and saw the tests catch each, and found one limit of the token after a release, below. The pace job, which gates nothing, was red on a slow runner in runs 130 and 131 (in run 130 four of fifteen under the floor, the job taking 622 seconds where a good runner takes 445); each time the lead counted the calls a thousand ticks make on the trunk and on the staged tree: the same to the call in run 130's tree, and in run 131's the same in one pace world and 130 fewer of 12.9 million in the other; so it was the runner. The builder's first report did not reach the lead (it had been put in the wrong field of the sending) and was sent again; and the owner corrected the lead for reading a builder's estimate of a run's length as a deadline.

**Listed, not built.**
- The pause's own line in the log ("Say 'resume the <station>' or 'stand down the <station>'") is addressed to the human and is read by a model captain in its samples; it is in every recorded game with a pause, and is left.
- Over the MCP bridge a token sent while a `say` or a `stand_by` holds the bridge waits for it, up to the bridge's wait (fifty seconds by default): delayed, not lost.
